author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Aryna Sabalenka defeated American Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2 to reach her fourth consecutive U.S. Open final and move within one victory of a third straight title in New York.

The world No. 1 recovered from a tightly contested opening set and took control with her serve and first-strike power. Sabalenka finished with 29 winners and seven aces, limiting Pegula’s opportunities to extend rallies and preventing the American from building momentum in the second set.

Sabalenka will face either Coco Gauff or Elena Rybakina in Saturday’s championship match. The matchup gives her another chance to reinforce a dominant recent run at Flushing Meadows after winning the previous two tournaments.

A victory would make Sabalenka the first woman since Serena Williams to win three consecutive U.S. Open singles titles. In the Open era, only Williams and Chris Evert have completed that streak. Pegula’s loss ends another deep run at her home major after she reached the semifinals for a third straight year.
dek: The world No. 1 advanced 7-5, 6-2 and will play for a third consecutive title at Flushing Meadows.
headline: Sabalenka beats Pegula to reach fourth straight U.S. Open final
